verdict.rationale: Stripe's protocols are documented as open. ACP is 'open source and community-designed under the Apache 2.0 license' and businesses can 'implement the specification'. A hands-on probe shows mpp.dev serving the full MPP spec index to a plain GET, with governance docs, so no signup or agreement is needed to read it. The 'versioned' part is not evidenced, so coverage is partial rather than complete. missing for 10: explicit spec versioning/release history for ACP or MPP, a stated no-agreement guarantee for implementers.

support.subject: As a developer, the commerce protocol this product speaks is published as an open, versioned specification I can read and implement without signing anything

citations.quote: ACP is open source and community-designed under the Apache 2.0 license. Businesses can implement the specification to transact with any AI agent or payment processor.
the Machine Payments Protocol is published in the open — https://mpp.dev/ answers a plain GET with the full markdown spec index
is an open protocol that lets agents pay for your APIs and services programmatically without a checkout UI, co-authored by Stripe and Tempo
submitted to the IETF for MPP for machine-to-machine payments
